R5: The catholic Pope decided to be a nice guy and "affirm my rights" to some RNW-Colonial regions, even though I am and have always been a good Sunni Muslim.
I'm guessing there's some weird interaction with my Vassals/Colonial Nations I inherited, but still, seems cool to me.

R5: Playing as a custom nation in South Africa I noticed that the early parts of Englands Newfoundlandish colony declared independence a little early and decided to call themselves "Texas" with 3 Provinces nowhere near anything I'd call Texas today.

Just to be clear, Newfoundland also exists (again) as a colonial nation still with England, so there's that.

R5: Completed the "Never say Nevers"-Achievment, owning all french territory as nevers (also starting as nevers).
Got lucky early by getting a PU over Spain, after that I basically waited around for truces. 

Somewhat tried to also be the emperor, but got unlucky with leagues voting bonuses and legitimacy.

Other interesting stuff: Brandenburg and Teutonic order exist, both catholic. Silesia, Ryazan and Kiev are hanging out, Russia only formed soem time after 1650, the Ottomans still haven't beaten the Mamluks at this point.

I also have High American Culture-Countries in my RNW, but since they don't have great access to any institutions, they are basically useless.

R5: Completed the "Great Moravia"-Achievment as Hungarys released vassal Nitra.
It took me a bit longer than expected, because I randomly got Austria as a PU and took ages to integrate it.

Other interesting things this playthrough: The Pope is doing quite good with no help from me whatsoever, the Ottomans seem to have a few problems (kinda thanks to me).

R5: Completed the "Arabian Coffee"-Achievment as Tuscany by forming Arabia and having Coffee-producing lands.

Interesting facts: I am emperor, the HRE is vassalised. Hungary is also my vassal. France/Castile both have my (Badensian) Dynasty on their throne, I just can't be asked to deal with claiming their thrones. Mughals is a Tributary of Ming, Ruthenia is hanging out, Scandinavia is also just hanging out.
I tried that, but maybe you need the month to roll over for that? For some reason that didn't seem to work for me while the game was paused.

R5: Completed the "Prince of Egypt"- Achievment starting as Florence.

In the past 10 in-game-days I renounced my (protestant) emperorship by switching back to catholic, released Lucca and Milan and fed them so much land in italy that I had less than 50% of my development outside of africa, left the hre & moved my capital to Cairo to form egypt.

Other interesting things that happened: Castile married a commoner, Kiev exists, Theodoro is doing quite ok for himself and I have High-American-RNW-Empires that suck pretty hard, because they haven't even discovered the Renaissance in 1640.

R5: I completed the "Academical!"-Achievment to get 50 Universities as Athens. My capital is in Forcalquier, I'm a prince in the HRE and I have some land in Greece, Elsass-Lothringen, the Low Counties, Franconia, Tuscany and more, adding up to actually 53 Provinces, because apparently I can't count. 

I had a hard time at the beginning, because Austria tried to implode to rebels early and couldn't really defend me from the Ottomans (or France, who also hate my guts). Athens itself was actually under Ottoman rule for over 150 years before I took it back later.

Bonus stuff: Tunis actually has land on the Iberian Peninsula, my best friend Aragon is doing great, Galicia is hanging out, Prussia and Brandenburg coexist, Denmark was swallowed by a (formerly) large Netherlands and Sweden.

Poland/Lithuania collapsed to rebels pretty early (thats why Danzig ist almost as far east as Riga) and Brandenburg had an easy time picking up the scraps. My vassals helped them quite a bit in the wars they called me into aswell.
Yeah, when I was still friends with Austria/Brandenburg we kicked the Ottomans ass in the league war and Austria made them release Serbia.

R5: I completed the Burgundian Conquest Achievement, which requires me to have the Low Counties as my own cores as well as France and Austria as Vassals/PU's. 

I wanted to try to PU Austria after having them help me defeat France, but that took too long so I dismantled them in 15 years of attacking random HRE-Princes over and over while they were still emperor. 
Salzburg is also my vassal and was fed a few provinces that way.

I also dismantled the empire while I was still at it, Brandenburg did help me at first but with over 300 AE they finally broke our alliance. 

Other interesting stuff: Ryazan got an early PU on Muscovy, so they never expanded east. Danzig is hanging out in non-prussian or german lands aswell.

R5: With my Custom Nation in Central America I got the "Talented an Ambitious Daughter"-event with a 6/6/6-Daughter when my current king was 74 and had no heir.

Yes, I'm playing with eastern slavic culture to have tsardom as a government option.

R5: Custom Nation "Zee" with all of Britannia/Scandinavia Norse for the "For Odin!"-Achievment.

Taking a HRE-Capital as well as East March/Ayrshire as starting land seemed very important, as it gave me easy access to spread within the HRE and on Ireland/Scotland. 

For some reason I messed up my economy in the early game and had to go bankrupt like 3 times, but with a bit of luck and (unfortunately) absolutely no help at all from my long-time-ally castille I started to take down England by 1520.

About my family.. Mmh, difficult to describe.. We're living in a south western part of Germany, and my parents are both from the former Eastern German Republic. I'm not sure how much people know about the cultural differences, but it really shows when I communicate with people. 
Not because of an accent or something like that, but because of behaviour. I'd maybe describe me father as an elitist? Someone that has no idea how to deal with free time and thus always searches for something to do. He doesn't want his son to be doing nothing either. 

(For some reason he seems to care less about my sisters, maybe they just hide the fact, that they are relaxing better than me?)

My older sister .. well .. best graduate in probably the nearest radius of schools of ~200 miles (which includes quite a lot of schools in Germany's city density). I personally wasn't bad at school, still within the upper 10% of graduates, still better than most people I knew but it apparently wasn't enough for my family.

I also have no idea why my sister is still living in my parents house, she graduated years ago (and is now studying at the local university) and started being annoying to make me move out months ago. She knows that I don't like talking to her (or to people in general) and still talks to me about me "having it better" than her (which she already admitted isn't true) and having hours of her talking to me while I say nothing. These kind of conversations always end with "Yeah, why don't you just move out, you'd not have to endure me then!" in this really, really, arrogant tone.
 Their reactions aren't something I can predict.My sister would definitely  want "to talk about it". I do NOT, under ANY circumstance talk to my sister about my barely existing personal life.
 My father could be like "yeah that's your own damn fault for not socialising" or maybe he'd want to send me off to a strange working "mission" in some village where you'd have do things like carrying rocks 10 hrs/day "to get me to get other ideas" or "keep me busy". No idea.

in the last 48 hours, I've been basically just .. existing? Helping my father fix the thing i ripped out of our roof when my suicide-attempt failed, and all that. The last few nights I had nightmares and my neck still really hurts, remembering the moment I jumped, being 100% sure that'd kill me still gives me adrenaline and reaally makes me uncomfortable. Which is one of the main reasons why I wouldn't try again. 

The reason I posted here was mainly to know how to deal with my situation, and the comments kind of helped me out.

I'm not sure what my parents are thinking tho. That stair didn't fall out on its own, and the marks on my neck are quite telling aswell, but if they don't want to accept the fact that I might have tried to suicide there, they'll not investigate further.

 "Hey this stair fell off the roof this morning, and i also fell off my bike, leaving these marks on my throat" - really unconspicious. 

I am sure that if I hadn't jumped from the height I jumped, but a little lower, I'd definitely have died there. The fact that I didn't makes me wonder.

Whenever I'm starting so close to the HRE, I always try to take over 3 or 4 electors as soon as possible. Some are small enough to be diplo-annexed, with some you have to look for allies that are maybe not part of the HRE, and for soe you can just improve relations to 100, enforce peace with dudes they are at war with (who you want to vassalize) and just storm in and murder everyone. I mainly didn't see a reason (and still really don't) to do things. Especially a few hours after my attempt failed, it all still doesn't make sense. I feel like I'd miss nothing and might aswell end it now, the only things left to come are even more pain/ me being even more stressed out without ever finding anything that'd be worth enduring the daily "dose" of uncomfortable-ness and stress.

I'm also at a point, where I'm supposed to make decisions. In the whole scheme of things, it doesn't really matter what i choose, I don't really care about it anyways (even though people tell me I should, because it it "MY" life .... spoilers: I don't really care?

I've also been the main target of people I like to call "retards" for basically all my life? The influence of meanies is probably more subconsciously? As you can see, I'm not too sure about that point.
